title: Psalms Chapter 40 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 40 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 40 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 40.

questions.question: According to Psalms 40:1, what did the LORD do when the psalmist waited patiently?
options: He inclined unto me and heard my cry
He ignored my plea
He sent an angel
He gave me riches
questions.correctAnswer: He inclined unto me and heard my cry
questions.explanation: Psalms 40:1 states that the LORD inclined unto the psalmist and heard his cry because he waited patiently.

questions.question: In Psalms 40:2, from what did God bring the psalmist up?
options: A horrible pit and miry clay
A deep ocean
A burning fire
A dark cave
questions.correctAnswer: A horrible pit and miry clay
questions.explanation: Psalms 40:2 says God brought the psalmist up out of a horrible pit, out of the miry clay.

questions.question: What did God set the psalmist’s feet upon, according to Psalms 40:2?
options: A rock
A sandy beach
A mountain peak
A river bank
questions.correctAnswer: A rock
questions.explanation: Psalms 40:2 mentions that God set the psalmist’s feet upon a rock and established his goings.

questions.question: What has God put in the psalmist’s mouth as stated in Psalms 40:3?
options: A new song
A prayer
A prophecy
A lamentation
questions.correctAnswer: A new song
questions.explanation: Psalms 40:3 declares that God has put a new song in the psalmist’s mouth, even praise unto God.

questions.question: According to Psalms 40:4, who is blessed?
options: He that maketh the LORD his trust
He that is rich
He that is proud
He that turneth aside to lies
questions.correctAnswer: He that maketh the LORD his trust
questions.explanation: Psalms 40:4 states that blessed is the man who trusts in the LORD and does not respect the proud or those who turn aside to lies.

questions.question: What does Psalms 40:5 say about the number of God's wonderful works?
options: They are too many to be numbered
They are few and countable
They are only in the heavens
They are written in a book
questions.correctAnswer: They are too many to be numbered
questions.explanation: Psalms 40:5 explains that God's wonderful works and thoughts toward us cannot be reckoned up in order; they are more than can be numbered.

questions.question: According to Psalms 40:6, which offerings did God not desire?
options: Sacrifice and burnt offering
Grain offering
Peace offering
Thanksgiving offering
questions.correctAnswer: Sacrifice and burnt offering
questions.explanation: Psalms 40:6 states that God did not desire sacrifice, burnt offering, or sin offering.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 40:1 says the psalmist waited impatiently for the LORD.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 40:1 says the psalmist waited patiently for the LORD, not impatiently.

questions.question: True or False: In Psalms 40:3, many shall see the new song and trust in the LORD.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 40:3 states that many shall see the new song, fear, and trust in the LORD.

questions.question: What does Psalms 40:4 say the blessed man does NOT respect?
options: The proud and those who turn aside to lies
The poor and needy
The righteous and faithful
The humble and meek
questions.correctAnswer: The proud and those who turn aside to lies
questions.explanation: Psalms 40:4 says the blessed man maketh the LORD his trust and respects not the proud nor those who turn aside to lies.

questions.question: According to Psalms 40:5, if the psalmist were to declare God's works, what would happen?
options: They are more than can be numbered
They would all be forgotten
They would anger the LORD
They would be easy to recount
questions.correctAnswer: They are more than can be numbered
questions.explanation: Psalms 40:5 says if the psalmist would declare and speak of God's works, they are more than can be numbered.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 40:6 says God opened the psalmist’s ears.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 40:6 states 'mine ears hast thou opened,' indicating God opened the psalmist’s ears.

questions.question: Which comes first in Psalms 40:1-6: God hearing the psalmist's cry or God setting his feet upon a rock?
options: God hearing the psalmist's cry
God setting his feet upon a rock
Both happen simultaneously
Neither happens
questions.correctAnswer: God hearing the psalmist's cry
questions.explanation: Psalms 40:1 mentions God hearing the psalmist's cry first; Psalms 40:2 mentions God setting his feet upon a rock afterward.

questions.question: According to Psalms 40:3, what effect does the new song have on many people?
options: They see it, fear, and trust in the LORD
They ignore it
They become angry
They forget it quickly
questions.correctAnswer: They see it, fear, and trust in the LORD
questions.explanation: Psalms 40:3 says many shall see the new song, fear, and trust in the LORD.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 40:5 teaches that God's thoughts toward us can be fully counted and understood.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 40:5 explains God's thoughts toward us cannot be reckoned up in order; they are beyond numbering.

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 40 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 40 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Psalms 40:7-8, what attitude does the psalmist express toward God's will?
options: He delights to do God's will and has God's law within his heart
He struggles with obeying God's commands
He is indifferent to God's law
He only follows God's law when convenient
questions.correctAnswer: He delights to do God's will and has God's law within his heart
questions.explanation: Psalms 40:7-8 states, 'Then said I, Lo, I come... I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart.' This shows that the psalmist willingly embraces God's will and internalizes His law.

questions.question: How does Psalms 40:9-10 highlight the psalmist's approach to sharing God's righteousness and salvation?
options: He preaches openly and does not conceal God's lovingkindness and truth
He keeps God's righteousness to himself
He preaches only to small groups in secret
He doubts God's salvation and does not share it
questions.correctAnswer: He preaches openly and does not conceal God's lovingkindness and truth
questions.explanation: Verses 9 and 10 emphasize that the psalmist has 'preached righteousness in the great congregation' and 'has not concealed thy lovingkindness and thy truth,' showing openness and boldness in proclaiming God's works.

questions.question: What plea does the psalmist make in Psalms 40:11 regarding God's mercies?
options: Do not withhold tender mercies, let lovingkindness and truth preserve me
Remove all mercies so I can learn discipline
Give me only judgment without mercy
Hide your truth from me
questions.correctAnswer: Do not withhold tender mercies, let lovingkindness and truth preserve me
questions.explanation: Psalms 40:11 petitions God not to withhold tender mercies and asks that lovingkindness and truth 'continually preserve me,' highlighting the psalmist's dependence on God's steadfast care.

questions.question: What does Psalms 40:12 reveal about the psalmist's experience with sin and adversity?
options: Innumerable evils and iniquities surround him, causing his heart to fail
He has no troubles or sins to confess
He is victorious over all evils without struggle
He feels indifferent toward his sins
questions.correctAnswer: Innumerable evils and iniquities surround him, causing his heart to fail
questions.explanation: Verse 12 describes how 'innumerable evils have compassed me about' and 'mine iniquities have taken hold upon me,' leading to the psalmist's heart failing, which illustrates deep distress due to sin and adversity.

questions.question: What connection can be drawn between Psalms 40:7 and Psalms 40:9 regarding the psalmist’s mission?
options: The psalmist willingly comes to fulfill God's purpose and openly preaches righteousness
The psalmist resists God's call and hides his message
The psalmist is uncertain about preaching righteousness
The psalmist only prepares privately without public preaching
questions.correctAnswer: The psalmist willingly comes to fulfill God's purpose and openly preaches righteousness
questions.explanation: Verse 7 shows the psalmist saying, 'Lo, I come,' indicating readiness to serve, which connects with verse 9 where he declares openly preaching righteousness, showing active fulfillment of God's purpose.

questions.question: Based on Psalms 40:10-11, how does the psalmist illustrate the relationship between faithfulness and God's preservation?
options: Declaring God's faithfulness and lovingkindness leads to preservation by His truth
Ignoring God's faithfulness results in preservation
Concealing God's lovingkindness ensures protection
Faithfulness has no role in God's preservation
questions.correctAnswer: Declaring God's faithfulness and lovingkindness leads to preservation by His truth
questions.explanation: The psalmist declares God's faithfulness and lovingkindness openly (verse 10) and then asks God not to withhold tender mercies so that lovingkindness and truth preserve him (verse 11), linking proclamation of God's character with divine preservation.

questions.question: What practical Christian virtue is emphasized in Psalms 40:8 when the psalmist says, 'I delight to do thy will, O my God'?
options: Obedience and heartfelt commitment to God's law
Reluctance to follow God's commands
Seeking personal gain over God's will
Ignoring God's instructions
questions.correctAnswer: Obedience and heartfelt commitment to God's law
questions.explanation: Verse 8 shows joy in doing God's will and internalizing His law, which reflects obedience and sincere commitment—a key Christian virtue.

questions.question: How does Psalms 40:13 teach believers to respond in times of distress?
options: By asking the LORD to deliver quickly and to hasten help
By ignoring God and handling problems alone
By blaming others for their troubles
By giving up hope
questions.correctAnswer: By asking the LORD to deliver quickly and to hasten help
questions.explanation: The psalmist petitions God, saying 'Be pleased, O LORD, to deliver me: O LORD, make haste to help me,' instructing believers to seek God's timely assistance in distress (verse 13).

questions.question: What is the psalmist's attitude toward those who seek to harm him, as expressed in Psalms 40:14-15?
options: He asks God to shame and confound them for their evil intentions
He wishes them well despite their harm
He ignores their actions
He seeks revenge himself
questions.correctAnswer: He asks God to shame and confound them for their evil intentions
questions.explanation: Verses 14 and 15 contain requests that those who pursue the psalmist's destruction be put to shame and desolate as a result of their evil, showing reliance on God’s justice rather than personal revenge.

questions.question: According to Psalms 40:16, what should those who seek the LORD do?
options: Rejoice, be glad, and continually magnify the LORD
Remain silent and avoid praising God
Seek only material blessings
Ignore God's salvation
questions.correctAnswer: Rejoice, be glad, and continually magnify the LORD
questions.explanation: Verse 16 encourages all who seek and love God's salvation to rejoice, be glad, and continually magnify the LORD, emphasizing joyful worship and praise.

questions.question: How does Psalms 40:17 describe the psalmist's condition and God's response?
options: Though poor and needy, the LORD thinks upon him and is his help
He is wealthy and self-sufficient
God has forgotten him
He is proud and refuses God's help
questions.correctAnswer: Though poor and needy, the LORD thinks upon him and is his help
questions.explanation: Verse 17 shows humility ('I am poor and needy') coupled with confidence that God remembers him and acts as his help and deliverer.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 40:6 states that God desires sacrifice and burnt offerings above all else.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 40:6 explicitly says God did not desire sacrifice and burnt offerings but rather opened ears, indicating God's preference for obedience over ritual sacrifice.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 40:4 teaches that a blessed person trusts in the LORD and does not respect the proud or liars.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 4 states, 'Blessed is that man that maketh the LORD his trust, and respecteth not the proud, nor such as turn aside to lies,' showing trust in God and rejection of pride and deceit.

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 40:3, the new song given by God causes many to fear and trust in the LORD.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 3 says God 'hath put a new song in my mouth... many shall see it, and fear, and shall trust in the LORD,' indicating the new song draws others to reverence and trust.

questions.question: A believer struggling with guilt over many sins feels overwhelmed and unable to look up. Based on Psalms 40:12-13, what biblical truth offers hope?
options: Though surrounded by innumerable evils and unable to look up, the believer can call on the LORD to deliver and hasten help
The believer must hide their sins to avoid shame
Sins are too many to be forgiven
The believer should rely only on self for deliverance
questions.correctAnswer: Though surrounded by innumerable evils and unable to look up, the believer can call on the LORD to deliver and hasten help
questions.explanation: Verse 12 describes feeling overwhelmed by sins, but verse 13 encourages calling on God to deliver and hasten help, offering hope despite guilt and distress.

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 40 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 40.

questions.question: According to Psalms 40:13, what does the Psalmist ask the LORD to do?
options: Deliver him and make haste to help him
Bless his enemies
Give him wealth and honor
Raise up a king for Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Deliver him and make haste to help him
questions.explanation: Psalms 40:13 explicitly states, 'Be pleased, O LORD, to deliver me: O LORD, make haste to help me,' showing the Psalmist's urgent plea for God's deliverance and help.

questions.question: In Psalms 40:14, what is the fate desired for those who seek to destroy the Psalmist's soul?
options: That they be ashamed, confounded, driven backward, and put to shame
That they be forgiven and blessed
That they be rewarded with peace
That they be strengthened in faith
questions.correctAnswer: That they be ashamed, confounded, driven backward, and put to shame
questions.explanation: Verse 14 requests that those who seek to destroy the Psalmist be ashamed and confounded together, driven backward and put to shame, indicating a call for divine justice against adversaries.

questions.question: What does Psalms 40:15 say about those who mock the Psalmist with 'Aha, aha'?
options: That they be desolate as a reward of their shame
That they be rewarded for their joy
That they be granted mercy
That they be ignored
questions.correctAnswer: That they be desolate as a reward of their shame
questions.explanation: The verse pronounces a curse on mockers, wishing them to be desolate as a reward of their shame, reflecting the Psalmist's plea for vindication.

questions.question: According to Psalms 40:16, who should rejoice and be glad in the LORD?
options: All those that seek the LORD and love His salvation
Only the priests in the temple
The enemies of the Psalmist
The kings of the earth
questions.correctAnswer: All those that seek the LORD and love His salvation
questions.explanation: Verse 16 clearly states that all who seek God and love His salvation should rejoice and say continually, 'The LORD be magnified,' highlighting the communal joy in God's deliverance.

questions.question: In Psalms 40:17, how does the Psalmist describe himself and what is his confidence?
options: Poor and needy, yet the Lord thinks upon him as his help and deliverer
Rich and powerful, relying on his own strength
Wise and knowledgeable, trusting in human wisdom
A king with many followers, confident in his army
questions.correctAnswer: Poor and needy, yet the Lord thinks upon him as his help and deliverer
questions.explanation: The Psalmist humbly acknowledges his poverty and neediness but expresses confidence that the Lord considers him and acts as his help and deliverer.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage echoes the theme of God delivering the needy and poor as expressed in Psalms 40:17?
options: Psalm 34:6
Genesis 1:1
Exodus 20:12
Proverbs 3:5
questions.correctAnswer: Psalm 34:6
questions.explanation: Psalm 34:6 says, 'This poor man cried, and the LORD heard him, and saved him out of all his troubles,' which parallels Psalms 40:17's theme of God’s attentive help to the needy.

questions.question: What literary device is prominent in Psalms 40:14-15, where the Psalmist prays for the shame and confusion of his enemies?
options: Imprecatory prayer
Parable
Metaphor
Allegory
questions.correctAnswer: Imprecatory prayer
questions.explanation: Verses 14 and 15 contain imprecatory prayers, invoking curses or judgment upon enemies, a common biblical literary device expressing trust in divine justice.

questions.question: In Psalms 40:6, God declares He does not desire sacrifice and offering but has opened the Psalmist's ears. What Hebrew term best reflects the idea of 'opened mine ears' in this context?
options: Shema (hear/listen)
Shalom (peace)
Chesed (lovingkindness)
Emet (truth)
questions.correctAnswer: Shema (hear/listen)
questions.explanation: 'Shema' means to hear or listen and is key to understanding the phrase 'mine ears hast thou opened,' indicating God’s desire for obedience over ritual sacrifice.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage quotes Psalms 40:7-8 to describe Jesus’ obedience to God's will?
options: Hebrews 10:5-7
John 3:16
Romans 8:28
Acts 2:38
questions.correctAnswer: Hebrews 10:5-7
questions.explanation: Hebrews 10:5-7 quotes Psalms 40:6-8 to show Jesus fulfilling the desire of God for obedience rather than sacrifice, emphasizing His willing submission to God's will.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 40:12 describes the Psalmist’s iniquities as fewer than the hairs of his head.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 40:12 states that the Psalmist’s iniquities are more than the hairs of his head, indicating overwhelming guilt, so the statement is false.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 40:4 blesses the man who trusts in the LORD and does not respect the proud or those who turn aside to lies.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 4 blesses the man who trusts in the LORD and does not respect the proud nor those who turn aside to lies, affirming the value of righteous trust.

questions.question: How does Psalms 40:9 describe the Psalmist's public proclamation of righteousness?
options: He has preached righteousness in the great congregation without refraining his lips
He has kept righteousness secret in his heart only
He has preached only to the priests
He has refused to speak of righteousness
questions.correctAnswer: He has preached righteousness in the great congregation without refraining his lips
questions.explanation: The verse states the Psalmist has openly preached righteousness in the great congregation and has not refrained his lips, demonstrating bold public witness.

questions.question: Which theme from Psalms 40 is fulfilled in the New Testament in the person and work of Christ?
options: The obedient servant who delights to do God's will
The call for ritual sacrifices
The establishment of earthly kingdoms
The rejection of God's law
questions.correctAnswer: The obedient servant who delights to do God's will
questions.explanation: Psalms 40:7-8 anticipates the obedient servant motif fulfilled in Jesus Christ, who delights in doing God’s will, as explained in Hebrews 10:5-7.

questions.question: What cultural or historical context helps understand the plea in Psalms 40:13 for God to 'make haste to help me'?
options: Ancient Near Eastern kings often acted slowly, so urgent divine help was needed
The Psalmist was wealthy and did not need help
The Psalmist was speaking to a pagan deity
This was a common phrase in Babylonian creation myths
questions.correctAnswer: Ancient Near Eastern kings often acted slowly, so urgent divine help was needed
questions.explanation: In the ancient Near East, kings and gods were often petitioned urgently because human rulers could delay; thus, the Psalmist’s plea for God to hasten reflects this cultural understanding.

questions.question: In Psalms 40:16, what is the repeated phrase that expresses continual praise to the LORD?
options: 'The LORD be magnified'
'Hallelujah'
'Bless the LORD'
'Holy, holy, holy'
questions.correctAnswer: 'The LORD be magnified'
questions.explanation: Verse 16 ends with those who love salvation saying continually, 'The LORD be magnified,' expressing ongoing praise and exaltation.

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 40 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 40 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Psalms 40:2 teach about God's saving action in the life of the believer?
options: God raises the believer from a desperate condition and establishes their path securely
God leaves the believer in their sinful state to learn lessons
God requires strict sacrifices before delivering the believer
God saves only those who are without sin
questions.correctAnswer: God raises the believer from a desperate condition and establishes their path securely
questions.explanation: Psalms 40:2 states that God brought the psalmist up out of a horrible pit and set his feet upon a rock, establishing his goings, which reveals God's saving and stabilizing work in the believer's life.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is primarily emphasized in Psalms 40:5 when David speaks of God's works and thoughts?
options: God's omniscience and wondrous works
God's wrath towards sinners
God's impatience with human failure
God's indifference to human affairs
questions.correctAnswer: God's omniscience and wondrous works
questions.explanation: Psalms 40:5 highlights the multitude of God's wonderful works and His thoughts towards us, which cannot be fully enumerated, emphasizing God's infinite knowledge and creative power.

questions.question: What does Psalms 40:6 reveal about God's requirements for worship and sacrifice?
options: God does not desire sacrifice and offerings but has opened the ears of the worshipper
God demands numerous burnt offerings and sin offerings
God accepts only animal sacrifices
God requires strict adherence to ritual law for acceptance
questions.correctAnswer: God does not desire sacrifice and offerings but has opened the ears of the worshipper
questions.explanation: According to Psalms 40:6, God does not desire sacrifice and offerings but rather has opened the ears of the worshipper, indicating that obedience and listening to God's will are more important than ritual sacrifices.

questions.question: How does Psalms 40:8 express the psalmist's attitude toward God's law?
options: The psalmist delights in doing God's will and has His law within the heart
The psalmist struggles to obey God's law
The psalmist finds the law burdensome
The psalmist ignores the law
questions.correctAnswer: The psalmist delights in doing God's will and has His law within the heart
questions.explanation: Psalms 40:8 states 'I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart,' revealing a willing and joyful obedience to God's law as internalized by the psalmist.

questions.question: What combined doctrine is taught by Psalms 40:9 and Psalms 40:10 regarding the psalmist's proclamation?
options: The psalmist openly preaches righteousness and declares God's faithfulness and salvation to the congregation
The psalmist keeps God's righteousness secret from others
The psalmist focuses only on personal salvation
The psalmist refrains from speaking about God's truth
questions.correctAnswer: The psalmist openly preaches righteousness and declares God's faithfulness and salvation to the congregation
questions.explanation: Verses 9 and 10 together show that the psalmist has not refrained his lips but has declared God's righteousness, faithfulness, salvation, lovingkindness, and truth openly to the great congregation, emphasizing public proclamation.

questions.question: What plea does the psalmist make in Psalms 40:11 and what does it reveal about God's sustaining grace?
options: The psalmist asks God to continually preserve him with tender mercies and truth
The psalmist demands material blessings
The psalmist requests immediate judgment on enemies
The psalmist claims self-sufficiency
questions.correctAnswer: The psalmist asks God to continually preserve him with tender mercies and truth
questions.explanation: Psalms 40:11 shows the psalmist's request for God's lovingkindness and truth to continually preserve him, highlighting God's sustaining grace as essential for spiritual endurance.

questions.question: Which doctrine about human sinfulness and its effect on the believer is taught in Psalms 40:12?
options: Innumerable evils and iniquities surround and oppress the believer, causing spiritual fainting
Sin has no effect on the believer's heart
The believer is free from sin's consequences
Sin leads to immediate physical death only
questions.correctAnswer: Innumerable evils and iniquities surround and oppress the believer, causing spiritual fainting
questions.explanation: Psalms 40:12 describes how innumerable evils and iniquities have compassed the psalmist, causing his heart to fail, revealing the doctrine of the pervasive and debilitating nature of sin in human experience.

questions.question: How does Psalms 40:13 reflect the psalmist's dependence on God in times of distress?
options: The psalmist urgently pleads for God's deliverance and swift help
The psalmist resolves to rely on self-help
The psalmist doubts God's ability to save
The psalmist ignores his distress
questions.correctAnswer: The psalmist urgently pleads for God's deliverance and swift help
questions.explanation: Psalms 40:13 contains a direct plea for God to deliver and hasten to help, highlighting the believer's dependence on God's timely intervention in distress.

questions.question: What is the psalmist's request concerning his enemies in Psalms 40:14 and Psalms 40:15, and what does it teach about divine justice?
options: The psalmist asks that those who seek to destroy him be ashamed, confounded, and desolate as a just reward
The psalmist asks for mercy on his enemies
The psalmist ignores his enemies
The psalmist seeks to reconcile without justice
questions.correctAnswer: The psalmist asks that those who seek to destroy him be ashamed, confounded, and desolate as a just reward
questions.explanation: Verses 14 and 15 reveal the psalmist's plea for divine justice against his enemies who seek his destruction, requesting they be put to shame and desolate, demonstrating trust in God's righteous judgment.

questions.question: How does Psalms 40:16 express the appropriate response of those who seek and love God’s salvation?
options: They rejoice, are glad, and continually magnify the LORD
They hide their faith and remain silent
They complain about God's law
They rely on their own works
questions.correctAnswer: They rejoice, are glad, and continually magnify the LORD
questions.explanation: Psalms 40:16 calls for all who seek God to rejoice and be glad, and those who love His salvation to say continually, 'The LORD be magnified,' emphasizing joyful worship and praise.

questions.question: What truth about God's providential care for the needy is taught in Psalms 40:17?
options: Though poor and needy, the psalmist knows God thinks upon him as help and deliverer
God abandons the poor and needy
The psalmist depends solely on human aid
The psalmist is wealthy and self-sufficient
questions.correctAnswer: Though poor and needy, the psalmist knows God thinks upon him as help and deliverer
questions.explanation: Psalms 40:17 expresses the doctrine that God cares for the poor and needy, remembering them and serving as their help and deliverer, reinforcing divine providence and mercy.

questions.question: What combined teaching about obedience and proclamation is revealed by Psalms 40:7-10?
options: The psalmist willingly comes to do God's will and openly proclaims His righteousness and truth
The psalmist resists God's will and remains silent
The psalmist prioritizes sacrifices over obedience
The psalmist hides God's salvation
questions.correctAnswer: The psalmist willingly comes to do God's will and openly proclaims His righteousness and truth
questions.explanation: Verses 7-10 together emphasize the voluntary and joyful obedience of the psalmist to God's will and his open proclamation of God's righteousness, faithfulness, lovingkindness, and truth to the congregation.

questions.question: How does Psalms 40:3 contribute to the biblical theology of worship and testimony?
options: God puts a new song of praise in the mouth of the believer, inspiring others to fear and trust in the LORD
Worship is a private affair without public impact
New songs are unnecessary for worship
Fear of the LORD is discouraged
questions.correctAnswer: God puts a new song of praise in the mouth of the believer, inspiring others to fear and trust in the LORD
questions.explanation: Psalms 40:3 shows that God places a new song of praise in the psalmist's mouth, which many will see, fear, and trust in the LORD, illustrating how worship serves as public testimony that leads others to faith.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that Psalms 40 teaches that God only values ritual sacrifices. What does Psalms 40:6 actually teach about God's desire for sacrifice?
options: God does not desire sacrifice and offerings but desires obedience and attentive ears
God exclusively demands animal sacrifices
God ignores obedience and focuses only on rituals
God is indifferent to worship forms
questions.correctAnswer: God does not desire sacrifice and offerings but desires obedience and attentive ears
questions.explanation: Psalms 40:6 explicitly states that God did not desire sacrifice and burnt offerings but has opened the ears of the worshipper, emphasizing obedience over ritual, refuting the sceptic's claim.

questions.question: What doctrinal insight about trust and humility is taught in Psalms 40:4?
options: Blessed is the man who trusts the LORD and does not respect the proud or those who turn aside to lies
Trusting in wealth brings blessing
Pride is a virtue to be respected
Lies are acceptable if they achieve good ends
questions.correctAnswer: Blessed is the man who trusts the LORD and does not respect the proud or those who turn aside to lies
questions.explanation: Psalms 40:4 teaches that blessing comes to those who trust God and reject pride and falsehood, affirming doctrines of faith, humility, and truth.
